newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy finds new armoured vehicle in Venice probe.
newsitem.headline: Italy finds new armoured vehicle in Venice probe.

text.p: Italian police have found a home-made armoured vehicle similar to the one used by the Venetian separatist group that last week stormed the belltower of St Mark's Square demanding independence, investigators said on Monday.

The vehicle was uncovered near Padua in northeast Italy, some 40 km (25 miles) from the lagoon city of Venice where eight armed separatists last Friday occupied the famous belltower to demand independence from Italy.
Prosecutor Guido Papalia said the vehicle was discovered in the course of investigations into Friday's incident and almost certainly belonged to the same group.
On Monday, the 200th anniversary of the fall of the Venetian Republic, an unidentified man phoned the ANSA news agency in the northern city of Bologna to threaten further armed action.
"Glory to the heroes of the republic. We have struck and will strike again," the voice said.
A communique received on Sunday by ANSA's Rome office had claimed a victory for the "Venetian Liberation Army" and said it would challenge the Italian authorities again soon.

Venice, a centuries-old independent power known as the "Most Serene" republic, which ruled an area stretching down the Adriatic and into the Middle East, fell on May 12, 1797, when French forces entered the city under Napoleon Bonaparte.
Friday's bizarre siege lasted only five hours and was ended peacefully when police moved into the belltower.
